title: Remediate WebView Dropdown UX
summary: Improve WebView dropdown usability by exposing policy choices, grouping diagnostics tail targets, disclosing route overrides progressively, and showing disabled/empty explanations.
reason: The NN/g dropdown review found dropdowns being used to hide small policy choice sets, diagnostics targets that were hard to scan, dynamic empty selects without clear disabled states, and route/track controls that relied on compact dropdowns or title text where visible context was needed.
behavior_before: Settings wizard policy choices, queue ordering strategy, and diagnostics tail targets were compact dropdowns even when the full option set was short and important. Empty dynamic selectors could appear blank or actionable. File override route controls were always presented as dense selectors, and disabled exact-track controls relied primarily on title text.
behavior_after: Short policy choice sets render as visible radio-card groups backed by the existing source selects; diagnostics tail targets are grouped by task; dynamic selectors disable themselves with explanatory placeholder options when empty; route overrides sit behind an explicit disclosure; disabled exact-track controls include visible, aria-described reasons.
